question.text: This cavalry officer during the War of the First Coalition was promoted to Marshal of the Empire. He was later executed by firing squad for his support of Napoleon during the failed Battle of Waterloo.
question.clue: This Napoleonic Marshal, called "the Bravest of the Brave," called for a cavalry charge at Waterloo that some still blame for Napoleon's loss there.

swap.leadin: He was the father of Pepin the Short, and his grandson became the namesake of the Carolingian dynasty.
swap.text: Name this mayor of the palace who conquered the province of Aquitaine after defeating Muslim forces at the Battle of Tours.
swap.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

question.text: This tribe was first united under Clovis I of the Merovingian dynasty. Under Charlemagne, this tribe came to control large portions of western Europe.
question.clue: Another ruler of these people waited a year to smash in the head of a man who crushed a bishop's vase.

swap.leadin: Sir John Fastolfe and various troops of Lord Talbot abandoned the battle field after hearing rumors of this woman's arrival.
swap.text: Name this French patron saint known as the Maid of Orleans. She was burned at the stake in Rouen at age 19.
swap.answerHtml: Saint Joan of Arc [or Jeanne d'Arc; prompt on Joan]
swap.clue: This leader convinced Robert de Baudricourt to allow this person to go to Chinon.

question.text: This final French emperor was captured by the Germans at the Battle of Sedan, after which he was forced to abdicate his throne. He shares his name with his uncle, who ruled France from 1804 to 1815.
question.clue: While in power, he sent troops to support a Maronite rebellion in Lebanon and had bombs hurled at his carriage by Felice Orsini, a Carbonari angry over his defense of Rome against irridentists.

swap.leadin: A group of probably fictitious female arsonists during this government were known as the petroleuse (PET-roh-looz).
swap.text: Name this socialist regime that controlled a national capital before being crushed by the Third Republic under Adolphe Thiers (teerz) in 1871.
swap.clue: It saw the adoption of the Red Flag and the Republican Calendar.

question.leadin: The tide of this battle is alleged to have turned when the losing side ran from the battlefield in order to protect their camp and all the loot inside.
question.text: Name this battle in which Frankish infantry defeated forces under Abd ar-Rahman. It took place after an appeal by Odo the Great as an invading force approached the River Loire.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Tours (or the Battle of Poitiers; or the Battle of the Palace of the Martyrs)
question.clue: The opposing forces in this battle met between the Clain and Vienne rivers, and it occurred near the village of Moussais-la-bataille.

swap.text: The Catholic League fought against this group of French Protestants, who were given amnesty in the Edict of Nantes and later expelled by the Edict of Fontainebleau by Louis XIV.
swap.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

question.text: After Emile Zola's treatise J'Accuse! in support of him was published, he became a cause celebre, and it was discovered that an army intelligence officer forged much of the evidence against him. For 15 points-name this Jewish officer in the French army whose 1894 treason conviction became a rallying point for European anti-Semitism.
question.clue: This man was accused of imitating his own handwriting, or "autoforgery," to suggest that he was the author of a bordereau found by a housekeeper in a wastebasket.

swap.leadin: This dynasty lends its name to a period of reforms in Latin America that included replacing the old office of the corregidor with that of the intendant.
swap.text: Identify this dynasty. The first king of Spain from this dynasty was Philip V.
swap.answerHtml: House of Bourbon [or House of Borbon or Bourbon Dynasty or Bourbon Family]
swap.clue: The Hundred Days was a brief interruption of this dynasty's namesake "restoration," and this dynasty gained power in Spain under Philip V. One ruler from this dynasty revoked the Edict of Nantes, ending toleration of Protestants.

question.leadin: This city is home to a Roman amphitheatre and the Maison Caree, a well-preserved Roman temple.
question.text: Name this city in Southern France whose name is the origin of the name of a very common form of cloth.
question.clue: This city contains the best preserved Roman amphitheater in the world, as well as an almost completely intact Roman Temple, the Maison Carree, which now contains a tacky 3-D theater.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the American African offensive in World War II.
swap.text: Eisenhower made a deal with this notorious Nazi collaborator which allowed him to bypass fighting the Vichy forces and move his troops east towards Rommel's Afrika Korps.

question.text: De Gaulle was the first president of the French republic of this number.
question.clue: Mitterrand, like Georges Pompidou and Charles de Gaulle, presided over this republican government of France, which came into being in 1958 and is still around today under Nicolas Sarkozy.

swap.text: The Reign of Terror was aggravated by the publications of this radical journalist who published Le Pere Duchesne and became a figurehead for the sansculottes.
swap.clue: Known for circulating an image of a man holding a hatchet and a revolver and standing over a kneeling priest, he referred to himself as the original Pere Duchesne.

question.text: This 1382 revolution was put down after the army of Charles VI took care of the Mallotins Revolt in Paris. It was the culmination of protests by Rouen's guilds against decades of high taxes levied to help fight the Hundred Years War.

swap.leadin: Horse manure and the microclimate created by this place caused the "pink of the fields" mushroom to be cultivated in the 1800s.
swap.text: Name this place to which bones from the Holy Innocents cemetery were transferred, stabilizing a sinking city.
swap.answerHtml: Paris catacombs [or Catacombs of Paris; or Catacombes de Paris]

question.text: The coronation of 25 French kings took place in this structure, modeled on Chartres Cathedral.
question.answer: Cathedral of Notre Dame of Reims
question.clue: In May 2013, Dominique Venner, an ultra-nationalist writer associated with Printemps Francais, shot himself inside this building in protest of France's gay marriage law.

swap.text: After initially refusing to take a position within the Directory, this politician eventually replaced Jean-Francois Rewbell and established control over the Directory in the Coup of 30 Prairial VII ("seven"). After the establishment of the Consulate, this politician served as second Consul alongside Napoleon and Roger Ducos.

question.text: Charles VII limited papal authority over the French church in this 1438 decree:
question.clue: Charles VII of France issued this pragmatic sanction in 1438, effectively instituting a modified version of the reforms proposed at the Council of Basel. Louis XI later repealed it.

swap.leadin: During this event, Archbishop Georges Darboy was executed.
swap.text: Name this May 1871 event which saw forces under Patrice de Mac-Mahon lead troops in vicious street fighting around Paris. It saw thousands killed at the Communards' Wall, many imprisoned at Versailles, and others deported to New Caledonia.
swap.answerHtml: Bloody Week [prompt on Paris Commune, accept La Semaine Sanglante]
swap.clue: This event that began on May 21, 1871, featured a massacre at Pere Lachaise (lah-SHEZ) Cemetery, and ultimately suppressed the Paris Commune.
